native_mechanisms: A single bone-colored die-stone (accumulator) is never reset between marks, so every fold carries the accumulated state of all prior folds.
Each mark's weight is pressed into the stone's already-turned position rather than a clean face, so earlier marks bend how later marks land (chained, order-dependent, amplifying dependence).
Only the stone's final seated position, read against the wooden numbered keeps (finalizer), ever leaves the desk; all intermediate turns and residue are discarded.
core_technique: Single 64-bit accumulator polynomial/LCG fold h = (h + word) * odd_P over 8-byte words (with an invertible v^(v>>47) pre-mix, length injected last), reassociated into four strided lanes with Q = P^4 for instruction-level parallelism, then a Moremur multiply-xorshift finalizer — i.e. FNV/xxHash-style multiply-mix-through-one-accumulator plus a textbook ILP unrolling.
